chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) for how long a child is prayed over if it reaches a certain number of years and months.
He said: 'Prayer is performed over it in all cases, unless it is omitted due to not being complete.'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning in these narrations is what we presented earlier in the narration of Abdillah ibn Sinan, [it is] the same.

key_terms.لِغَيْرِ تَمَامٍ: Due to not being complete (referring to age/maturity)
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: Prayer is performed over him (funeral prayer)

ai.seo_question: At what age or stage of development is funeral prayer performed over a deceased child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes that funeral prayer is obligatory for a child regardless of age, with the exception of infants who have not yet reached 'completeness' (kamal), a state often interpreted as the expulsion of the soul or distinct physical maturity. Shaykh al-Tusi notes that this ruling harmonizes with the precedent set by Abdullah ibn Sinan, reinforcing the consistency of the Imams' jurisprudence on the ritual purification and prayer for the deceased, even in early childhood.
